$comment: D-PP-EMBED-PARAMS (C23 6.10.4.2-6.10.4.5), closed P60: runtime witness for the standard `#embed` parameters -- limit / prefix / suffix / if_empty, the `__limit__` spelling (6.10.1p5), a macro-expanded limit clause (6.10.4.2p3), and `__has_embed`'s three answers with parameters (6.10.2p7, EXAMPLE 6), including C23 6.10.2 EXAMPLE 5's vendor guard crossed with EXAMPLE 6's limit (`ds9000::element_type(short) limit(2 - 3)`), which an implementation that evaluates the limit BEFORE testing for an unrecognized prefixed parameter cannot compile at all (6.10.1p9 footnote 196 + 6.10.2p8 NOTE 1) -- RUN on BOTH the baseline (debug) AND the `release` (shippedPipeline) arm. payload.bin (40 bytes, hostile bytes first: 2A 0D 0A 1A 00 FF 80 7F, then 8..39) is LONGER than every limit used, so a limit that is ignored produces a different element count AND different bytes. Each array's size and every byte is checked (distinct exit codes 1..9 on a mismatch) before the final `(sum(head) + all[39] + four[3]) & 0xFF` = 203 is returned through a runtime-opaque index (the anti-fold pattern), so the release arm proves the embedded arrays are materialized and indexed at runtime. ⚠ NO REFERENCE COMPILER CAN COMPILE THIS FILE: gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and MSVC 19.51.36252 refuse `#embed` entirely (MEASURED 2026-09-04, each separately, plain quoted `#embed` as the control), so the oracle here is the ISO C23 text (N3220), cited clause by clause in main.c.
